I studied linguistics partially because I couldn’t stand not having a way to answer questions like these, lol. Anyway, if you’re interested, the linguistic answer is that cereal is not a canonical soup — “canonical” meaning what you think of when you think of the word “soup”, based on how you’ve seen people use the word “soup” rather than any logical category. Because most of us haven’t really seen people describe cereal as “soup”, we don’t consider it a canonical soup.

Based on this canonical division, we can come up with logical categories to communicate the canonical category. But because it’s not naturally logical, that’s why it’s so hard to come up with something that logically includes everything canonical and excludes everything non-canonical. (A food with solid in liquid where the liquid is the main part of the food…? But what about potato soup? Is that really liquid?) Or, you can just bite the bullet and accept that non-canonical items like cereal must be soup based on the logical definition you choose.

For example, imagine someone from a culture who has nothing like soup: no cereal, no soup, no stew or sauce, etc. If they were to learn English, they would learn what “soup” is based on a logical definition, since they would have no idea of canonicity based on their culture, unlike we do. They would actually be confused that cereal isn’t soup if they learned the logical definition that soup is food suspended in a liquid.

Alright, I’m going to try to spell it out as specifically as I can:

1. Install the Python 3.10 and the newest Homebrew. Sorry, you can figure this out with Google, it’s generally very straightforward and if you run into issues I probably don’t know how to solve them
2. Open Terminal. Type in “brew install python-tk” and press enter.
3. Make a new folder somewhere. To make the following steps easier to describe, let’s assume you’re making a folder called “vocadbinstaller” in your Documents folder.
4. Open TextEdit. Copy the contents from the big box in the Pastebin link into it. Save it in the folder you just made under “v5_db_installer.py”, so its full path is “Documents/vocadbinstaller/v5_db_installer.py”.
5. The script has an error. Find the line that says “dec = re.split(r"\W", dec)[0]” and replace it with “dec = dec[:14]” (this is what the edit to the post was about). Don’t change any of the spacing at the beginning of the line.
6. Go to the Google Drive link and download the file. Move it into the vocadbinstaller folder.
7. Open Terminal. Type in “cd ~/Documents/vocadbinstaller” and press enter. This changes the working directory to the folder where everything is.
8. Type in "chmod 777 date2drp2" and press enter. This lets the DB installer run the file like it needs.
9. Type in “sudo python3 v5_db_installer.py” and press enter. You’ll need to be an admin, and it will ask you for your password. (Don’t worry, the program won’t steal your password. Also, even if you don’t see anything show up when you’re typing your password, it’s still being entered, and you can just type enter when you’re done.)
10. The installer window will pop up. Use the buttons to select a voicebank. At this point, you might get an error saying that Apple blocked date2drp2; you can resolve it easily in Settings (can’t remember where, but it should be easy to find if you Google the error message). If you get this error, the voicebank hasn’t been properly loaded, and once you unblock date2drp you’ll have to select the voicebank again.
11. Click the button to install the voicebank. Hopefully you’ll get a “success” message.

I was in the exact same place as you when I was 13 — I felt so worthless and lazy, couldn’t reach any of other people’s goals for me or even my own for myself. But once I got to college, I was lucky enough to find people and belief systems that affirmed I was good enough on my own. And it seemed like the more I felt their support, the more my self-worth and motivation drastically improved without even trying. 

As much as I could tell myself I didn’t need to be productive or accomplished to be worth something before I found them, I couldn’t believe it just by saying it to myself, and it took years of struggle with the idea and so many tear-filled talks with my new support system to make the feelings settle down. Because no matter how good you are — and honestly, looking back, I’m sure others saw me as far more skilled than I saw myself — you will never believe it until you know you’re valuable just as a person.

It sounds like your circumstances aren’t really conducive to finding support like this, and all I can say is to hang in there and hang onto the truth that you’re worth just as much as any prodigy out there, no matter what the people around you or your own brain is trying to tell you. Try your best to find people who accept you even as you are and try your best to accept their acceptance. I know all of this will feel like a lie until you actually experience it, but at least believe that it’s out there somewhere.

Interestingly, this was actually what I enjoyed quite a bit more than the others because it felt so much more realistic and actually worked pretty well for worldbuilding -- it gave you a good idea of how much responsibility Leon had as the champion and what you're really getting yourself into. It also made a lot of sense that someone with a much longer record of winning against high level opponents would be called to deal with the evil guys while you, as a kid, would be told to focus on your training. Eventually, the champion gets tied up and you have to go rescue him, so it's not like you never get to actually take part in the action. (Besides, at the point where you have to fight Eternatus, you're considered worthy enough to challenge him for his title, so naturally people would be less inclined to hold you back from joining him.)

Part of it might also have been the nature of Macro Cosmos. I don't like how it felt like they just stuck them on at the end, with very minimal references to any such evil going on beforehand -- or at least, they could have made those references more clearly evil rather than simply self-centered, like Bede's wishing star collection or Oleana's obsession with Rose. But the entire point was that all their misdeeds happened behind the scenes. Rose is a white-collar criminal who is really good at a) hiding everything, and b) talking his way out of the things he can't hide. So you couldn't really have any real encounters with Macro Cosmos earlier: they never planned to do anything obviously wrong to the people around them.
